 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. New York Giants fans may be wishing for a Jonathan Taylor trade, but ESPN's Bill Barnwell suggested a cheaper alternative for the running-back-needy team.
 Barnwell floated Derrick Henry as a viable trade option for the Giants, which would reunite the Baltimore Ravens' future Hall of Fame running back with his with his former coach, John Harbaugh, now in his first season leading the Giants.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Giants are among five teams that have been linked to Taylor, the Indianapolis Colts' superstar running back, via a trade ahead of the NFL's 4 p.m. ET deadline on Tuesday, Nov. 10.
 The Giants need the help. They are down to one healthy running back with NFL carries on their roster, Devin Singletary, and are working hard to upgrade the position before next week.
 ESPN Analyst Floats Derrick Henry as a Giants Trade Candidate
 The Colts are reportedly seeking a first-round draft pick in exchange for the 2021 rushing champion, and the Giants are already down their fourth-, fifth- and seventh-round draft picks for 2027.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But Henry, 32, is four years older than Taylor and signed through the 2027 season, unlike Taylor who is locked in through 2028. That means Henry could be cheaper in a trade and definitely would take up less than Taylor's $22 million cap hit.
 The Ravens could also be inclined to trade the back amid their cratering season, where they lost quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries.
 "Taylor might cost too much for a New York squad that's already down its fourth- and fifth-round picks in the 2027 draft, but what about Derrick Henry?" Barnwell wrote for ESPN.com on Thursday. "If the Ravens decide their season is up without Lamar Jackson on the field, Henry could be a potential trade candidate. He's owed only $650,000 over the rest of 2026 and $12 million in 2027."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Could a Trade Invigorate Derrick Henry?
 Henry has dominated in his first two seasons in Baltimore, surpassing 1,500 yards in both 2024 and 2025. Despite leading the NFL in carries (158), Henry is only averaging 4.0 yards per carry this year, far down from his 2024 (5.9) and 2025 (5.2) marks.
 But the Ravens' awful quarterback play has had a hand in Henry's drop-off. The running back averaged 95.2 yards per game over Baltimore's 4-1 start, but he has failed to reach even 60 yards over Baltimore's three-game losing streak.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement But being reunited with Harbaugh, in a run-first offense with RPO-style quarterback J.J. McCarthy, could invigorate Henry, according to Barnwell.
 "While the future Hall of Famer has struggled for most of the season, playing with a more mobile quarterback in McCarthy might help create some running lanes," Barnwell said.
